newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain, Belgium heal extradition rift.
newsitem.headline: Spain, Belgium heal extradition rift.

text.p: Spain and Belgium smoothed over a diplomatic row on extradition on Tuesday and agreed to improve cooperation in the fight against terrorism and organised crime.

"These resolutions are testimony to their common will to put the security of citizens and of victims of terrorism and well as sexual violence in the centre of their concerns," ministers from both countries said in a joint statement in Madrid.

The two European Union states hope the accord will let them re-start full cooperation on extradition requests in the "shortest time possible", before ratification of an EU-wide treaty to be signed in Dublin on Friday.
The two countries came to diplomatic blows in February when Spain broke off judicial relations following a Belgian court's refusal to extradite two alleged Basque separatist activists.

"There have been difficult relations between Belgium and Spain that were exceptional in nature," Spain's Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja told a news conference. "With this bilateral accord, Belgium and Spain will start cooperation before the other European countries."
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) have killed some 800 people since 1968, when they started a violent drive for Basque independence.
